title: Pattern matching
description:
Complete the methods with switch expressions and patterns:

```csharp
public static string Describe(object? value)
public static decimal TicketPrice(int? age, bool student)
public static string Summarize(int[] values)
```

`Describe` returns:
- `"nothing"` for `null`
- `"zero"` for the int 0, `"negative int"` / `"positive int"` for other ints
- `"empty text"` for `""`, otherwise `"text of length N"` for a string
- `"list of N"` for any `List<int>`
- `"something else"` for anything else

`TicketPrice` (in euros): an unknown age (`null`) pays 12; under 4 pays 0; 4 to 12 pays 6; 65 and over pays 7; students aged 13 to 25 pay 8; everyone else pays 12.

`Summarize` uses list patterns: `"none"` for an empty array, `"just N"` for one item, `"N and M"` for two, and `"F ... L (K items)"` for more, with the first, last and count.
hints: Switch on a tuple to test two values at once: `(age, student) switch { (null, _) => ..., (< 4, _) => ... }`. Arms are tried in order, so each later arm only sees the ages the earlier ones did not take.
Order matters in `Describe` as well: the constant `0` must come before the general `int n`, and `""` before `string s`.
